video_title: Draymond Green Reacts To Steph Curry Story, Potential Bucks Penalty & JJ Redick's Lakers Comments

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Steph Curry's rare eye condition during the 2018 Warriors championship run
quotes.excerpt: Steph says he suffered from a rare eye condition during the Warriors dynasty run.
quotes.quote: Steph says he suffered from a rare eye condition during the Warriors dynasty run. It was 2018. Bob Myers texted me after the game because apparently the telecast kept showing me when I was on the bench and he was like, 'You're just squinting, looking like you couldn't see anything. You should probably go get that checked out.' They told me that I had a rare condition called keratoconus. I remember Steph saying this word before. I don't know if that's the right pronunciation, so internet, thesauruses, and grammar police, excuse me if I'm wrong. What I found out about it was it's a progressive condition that can deteriorate your vision over time and it's irreversible if it goes in the wrong direction. I joked that when I'm done, my memoir should be called 'The Whole Time I Couldn't See.'

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the Milwaukee Bucks' potential salary cap circumvention investigation
quotes.excerpt: This really would set the Milwaukee Bucks franchise back.
quotes.quote: The Bucks are reportedly being investigated by the NBA for possible salary cap circumvention in the deal with Gary Trent Jr. The punishment could be equally as severe, if not worse than the Clippers' punishment if found guilty. No way this could be a worse punishment, because I guess when you think about it, it is circumvention, because you could get a player for cheap. But it's not the same. I do think the punishment will be strenuous, but this really would set the Milwaukee Bucks franchise back. And I think if this was to happen, I think the Bucks owner would then sell, because unlike Steve Ballmer, who's the wealthiest owner, unlike Steve Ballmer who has a team that's in Los Angeles, the Milwaukee Bucks lose five first-round draft picks and they can never be good for 20 years. So I think you'd see that owner sell the team if this is the case.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on JJ Redick's comments about the Lakers' roster fit
quotes.excerpt: I understand what he's saying when he says the pieces fit together better.
quotes.quote: JJ Redick said in his press conference, 'I think we've always tried to give our players clearly defined roles and I think with this group, it's probably the first time in my three years here that I feel like the pieces actually fit together.' I know everybody takes this as a shot at LeBron and be like, 'Oh man, he's talking about LeBron leaving,' and I don't think so. If you think the last two years with LeBron and Luka, that really wasn't a fit. So you have that. Before that, I don't necessarily know what pieces didn't fit, but LeBron and Luka are both ball-dominant players and LeBron had to learn how to play without the ball. And I ultimately don't think it allowed for the best LeBron James. So I understand what he's saying when he says the pieces fit together better because they've built a team that's heavily going to play roles with Luka having the ball.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on Trae Young's comments about his Atlanta Hawks teammates
quotes.excerpt: Even with a teammate that can draw double teams, it's still not that easy to win.
quotes.quote: Trae Young had a quote about why he never won with the Atlanta Hawks. He said, 'I don't know if I've ever had a teammate that can draw double teams like this,' referring to Anthony Davis. Well, what I will say to Trae Young is, even with a teammate that can draw double teams, it's still not that easy to win. It is very tough to win. I get what he's saying. He's saying the level of teammates he had. And I agree by the way. I think when you go back to this podcast, when the Atlanta Hawks beat the New York Knicks, I said then, 'Listen, people are going to get excited about this Hawks team and it's really not a conference finals team.' And everybody did, and you saw that it really wasn't a conference finals team. They had a good year, a lot like the Portland Trail Blazers did some years back when they had that really good year and we mopped them in the conference finals.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Smart's comments on the Lakers' contract offer
quotes.excerpt: It wasn't any security that we wanted that they were willing to do.
quotes.quote: Marcus Smart made a quote about choosing the Rockets over a disrespectful offer from the Lakers. He said, 'First off, I played so well that the offer that was ultimately given didn't match the way that I played, especially when you see guys who played way worse than I did, the offers they're getting.' And then it wasn't any security that we wanted that they were willing to do. What I would take away from this quote and what I think the most important part about this quote is, is the security that Marcus Smart wanted. Because Marcus Smart should know that in this league, it ain't always about who played better. For instance, he may have played better than Austin Reaves in the playoffs. They ain't giving Marcus Smart Austin Reaves' money because he played better than Austin Reaves in the playoffs. That's just not how the NBA works. Paul Reed played better than Jaylen Brown in the playoffs last year. They're not paying Paul Reed Jaylen Brown's money.
